In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the carcinogenic potential of particle-associated PAHs is determined by the combined effect of the properties of the PAHs, their carrier particles and the conditions in the BLL.
the lipids in surfactant are not only important in maintaining normal lung function, but also in protecting the lung against the carcinogenic action of PAHs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the carcinogenicity of PAHs associated with particles is determined by the rate of transport through the lipid-aqueoous heterogeneity of the bronchol lining layer, the lipids being the main rate-determining component.
the lipids in the surfactant system are important in protecting the lungs from the action of carcinogens.

the carcinogenic potency of particle-associated polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons is determined not only by their physical properties but also by their interaction with the lipids in the lining layer of the bronchus.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the lipid-aquaeus structure of the bronchiolal lining layer (BBL) may be the major determinant in the overall transport rate of particle-associated PAHs from the airway lumen to the bronchus epithelium.

the enhanced carcinogenicity due to the association of PAHs with particulate matter is not due to the prolonged retention of the hydrocarbons, but to the prolonged retention in the lipid phase of the bronchogenic epithelium.
the enhanced carcinogenicity associated with particle-associated PAHs can not be explained simply by the slow release of PAHs.
